lead: Test build 0.8.30 (CI run CIRUN). New in this round: the MATRIX page's destination menus list Distortion Mix, Osc 1/2 F-Shift and Osc 1/2 F-Spread and show them after a reload (issue #11, E309); the Control Center restores a RAM bank from a backup, RAM only (Restore... / RESTORE in the Access look, E313); on Linux the broker resets the USB port before it gives the Virus back (E312). Linux: #11 and the restore were tested on dev builds; hil.sh runs the core items on this CI build. Mark each item, add a note where something looks different, then copy the results at the bottom into the chat.
rules: Never store a patch on the Virus with the Virus' own STORE button.
Restore tests write into the Virus' RAM: first make a fresh backup (Backup button), change only RAM A slots 24-31, then restore RAM A from that fresh backup. Never restore an older backup.
Order: Linux first (the Virus is on this PC), then the Windows 11 VM, then macOS. Close the DAW before the Virus moves.

sections.title: Linux
sections.where: REAPER via pw-jack, Virus on this PC
prep: Already installed by Claude: the CI build (install.sh).
Claude runs hil.sh on this build (cold start, reopen x2, export, broker kill) and reports the result here; the broker's give-back (E312) runs at every reopen.

items.title: Mod matrix destinations (#11)
steps: MATRIX page, slot 1: open the destination menu and choose Osc 2 F-Shift; slot 2: Distortion Mix.
Save the project, close REAPER, open the project again and look at the MATRIX page.
items.expect: the menu has Distortion Mix, Osc 1/2 F-Shift and Osc 1/2 F-Spread and no '-reserved-' entries; the Virus' display names the destination; after the reload both fields still show them.

items.title: Control Center: backup and restore
steps: TI Revive Control Center (plain view): Backup (a new folder under Documents/Access Music/Virus TI/Backups).
In the plug-in's browser drag one patch from a library onto RAM A slot 24.
Control Center: Restore..., choose the new backup's RAM A.mid, then 'Overwrite RAM A with ...'.
items.expect: the status line says RAM A was restored, 1 programs written; slot 24 has its old name again in the browser (after Download entire bank if needed).

sections.title: Windows 11 VM
sections.where: win11 VM, Ableton Live 11, Virus attached by Claude
prep: Already installed by Claude: setup.exe /quiet (entry 0.8.30, same plug-in as the CI MSI), C:\tirevive-test\0.8.30-ci.
Ask Claude to attach the Virus to the VM (it stops the Linux broker first).

items.title: Mod matrix destinations (#11)
steps: MATRIX page, slot 1: choose Osc 1 F-Spread in the destination menu.
items.expect: the menu has Distortion Mix, Osc 1/2 F-Shift and Osc 1/2 F-Spread and no '-reserved-' entries; the field shows Osc 1 F-Spread.

items.title: Control Center in the Access look: RESTORE
steps: TI Revive Control Center in the Access look: BACKUP, then OK (a new folder under Documents/Access Music/Virus TI/Backups).
In the plug-in's browser drag one patch onto RAM A slot 25.
Control Center: RESTORE, choose the new backup's RAM A.mid, then 'Overwrite RAM A with ...'.
items.expect: the status says RAM A was restored, 1 programs written; slot 25 has its old patch again.

sections.title: macOS
prep: Claude copies the package (CI run CIRUN) to ~/Downloads/TI-Revive-0.8.30-ci-mac when the Mac is awake; double-click 'Install test build.command' there (the command is in INSTALL-COMMAND.txt). Virus on the Mac.
Claude puts diag.on in the plug-in's folder and renames the old diag.log.

items.expect: the menu has Distortion Mix, Osc 1/2 F-Shift and Osc 1/2 F-Spread and no '-reserved-' entries; both fields show the choice.

items.title: Control Center in the Access look: RESTORE
steps: TI Revive Control Center in the Access look: BACKUP, then OK (a new folder under Documents/Access Music/Virus TI/Backups).
In the plug-in's browser drag one patch onto RAM A slot 26.
Control Center: RESTORE, choose the new backup's RAM A.mid, then 'Overwrite RAM A with ...'.
items.expect: the status says RAM A was restored, 1 programs written; slot 26 has its old patch again.
